title: Minuta 2026-03-26
summary: The minutes of the 26 March meeting record the 25bp cut to 6.75% by a 3-2 majority and show a Board more divided, and on balance more hawkish, than the bare communique conveys. The three cutters lean on transitory supply shocks (jitomate, Middle East energy buffered by the gasoline price cap), widening slack and a rate still above historical references, but one frames the move as 'cerca de concluir el proceso de normalización' and sees margin for just one additional adjustment. The two dissents are substantive: Borja says the ex-ante real rate is already within the neutral range, and Heath wants a pause through at least the first half of 2026 and warns that cutting signals weaker commitment to the mandate; the majority keeps the inflation risk balance tilted up, with one member seeing that bias increased significantly. Versus the previous minutes (February), where the majority framed the pause as temporary and pressed to resume easing, the Board did resume cutting but the debate shifted toward how close the cycle is to its end. Net, a divided, late-cycle cut with room for at most one more move, half a notch less dovish than the communique.

key_quotes.quote: Consideró que hacia delante existe margen para realizar un ajuste adicional en congruencia con el entorno macroeconómico del país.
key_quotes.context: A cutter sees room for one more adjustment, after calling the stance close to the end of normalization

key_quotes.quote: Argumentó que se necesita implementar una pausa en la postura actual al menos durante la primera mitad de 2026, con el fin de evaluar si los choques inflacionarios existentes se han absorbido.
key_quotes.context: Heath's hawkish dissent: pause at least through H1 2026

key_quotes.quote: Desde noviembre, la tasa de interés real ex ante se ubica dentro del rango estimado como neutral y está muy cerca de su estimación central.
key_quotes.context: Borja's dissent: the stance is already near neutral, so hold to assess the shock

key_quotes.quote: La mayoría enfatizó que el incremento en los precios de dichos productos agrícolas se asocia con un choque de oferta transitorio.
key_quotes.context: The majority looks through the fruit-and-vegetable spike that drove headline to 4.63%
